overview: White brings the queen to d3 on move three, eyeing the b5 and h7 squares and keeping the c-pawn flexible. It is a very rare line that blocks White's own bishop and knights, and Black simply develops with ...e6, ...c5 or ...Bf5 and gets an easy game. I am unsure of the details; the queen on d3 gives Black comfortable play.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bf4, e3, O-O-O and use the queen on d3 to eye h7 and b5.
Keep options for e4 and Nb5 ideas against c7.

black_ideas.idea: Develop naturally with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Bf5, hitting the queen with tempo.
Strike with ...c5 or ...e5 to exploit White's awkward piece placement.

typical_structures.structure: Queen's Pawn structure with White d4 and Black d5, a flexible centre and a misplaced queen.

character.notes: Awkward and quiet; Black develops with tempo and risk is small.

soundness.notes: Passive and loses time but not outright refuted.

structure.notes: Both sides keep the centre tension and options open.

approach.notes: A very rare queen sortie that strong players do not play.

level.notes: Few theory demands but a poor repertoire choice.

character.reason: Quiet but awkward play with no forcing lines.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and both sides keep options.

level.reason: Simple moves but a poor first repertoire.

plans.reason: White's queen comes out to d3 on move three.
